Pinterest Marketing for Print on Demand and Custom Shops

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

A custom product shop has a special Pinterest problem: lots of items that look alike. A dozen shirt designs, a range of tumblers, a stack of transfers in different themes. If you pin each product once with its product name, you have used a fraction of what Pinterest can do for you. Pinterest marketing for a print on demand shop starts by thinking in searches, not in SKUs.

Why one pin per product is not enough

A single pin can match a single search, and most products are searched for in more than one way. One design might be found by someone shopping for a teacher gift, by someone decorating a classroom, and by someone who loves the theme itself. One pin cannot serve all three. It also means your catalog is limited to as many pins as you have products, no matter how many searches your buyers actually run.

Think in angles: occasion, audience, theme

For each product idea, list the different reasons someone might look for it.

Occasion

Holidays, graduations, birthdays, back to school, a season, a team event.

Audience

Who wears it, gives it or uses it: teachers, new moms, coaches, a book club, a group of friends.

Theme

The subject of the design itself: a humorous saying, a favorite book world, a hobby, a holiday motif.

Each angle becomes its own keyword. A tumbler and a shirt can share a theme but be pinned to different audiences, so your keyword list grows far beyond product names. Our guide to long tail keywords on Pinterest shows how to shape these phrases.

Two distinct pins per product idea

A workable standard for a shop like this is two distinct pins per product idea. Distinct does not mean the same image in two colors. It means:

  • A different keyword and title, aimed at a different search.
  • A different image concept, such as a clean product view and a styled or in-use view.
  • A different description that speaks to that angle.

Mockups, photos of the finished item and lifestyle images all count as different concepts. Keep the destination accurate: a pin about one design goes to that product page, and a pin about a theme can go to the collection that holds several.

Boards for a catalog of similar items

Name boards for the shopper's search, not for your product type. "Teacher gift ideas" and "funny mom shirts" are searchable topics, while "Shirts, batch 4" is not. A single design can appear on more than one board when it genuinely fits each topic. The Pinterest SEO for Shopify stores post covers how to connect boards, collections and product pages.

Keep a simple tracking sheet

With many similar products, a spreadsheet keeps you from repeating yourself. Try these columns:

  1. Product or design name
  2. Occasion, audience and theme
  3. Target keyword for pin one and pin two
  4. Pin title and destination link
  5. Date published

Review it every month. Pins that earn saves and clicks show you which occasions and audiences to build on. Pinterest builds over weeks and months of consistent effort, so keep the sheet running rather than judging early.

Frequently asked questions

Why is one pin per product not enough for a print on demand shop?

One pin matches one search, but products are usually found by occasion, audience and theme. Several distinct pins per product idea let the same item be found through more than one route.

What makes two pins for the same product distinct?

A different keyword and title, a different image concept and a different description. Two pins with the same image in another color are still nearly the same pin.

How should a shop with hundreds of similar products organize boards?

Name boards for shopper searches, such as an occasion or an audience, rather than for product batches. A design can appear on several boards when it genuinely fits each topic, and each board should keep one clear theme.

Does Pinterest work for DTF transfer and custom product shops?

It can, because buyers search for ideas around occasions and themes before buying. Results take weeks or months of consistent effort and are never guaranteed, so it works best as a long term channel.
